source.title: From Latents to Wires: Surgical Post-Editing on Large Language Models
source.authors: Jiankai Jin; Xiang-Zheng Zhang; Zhao Liu; Wen-Zhuo Xu; Dong-Dong Yang; De-Yue Zhang; Quan-Chen Zou

record.tranche_reason: The study applies directional ablation based on a difference between mean residual activations for refusal and matched non-refusal prompts, projects the selected direction out at every layer and token position, and reports refusal and capability outcomes on three model configurations.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports L2W post-edit results and describes candidate-direction selection. Those are not recorded as rows: L2W is a separate method, and candidate-selection details are not outcomes of the direction itself. The reported directional-ablation table and its benchmark scores are recorded.
record.test_reason: Section 6.5, Table 6 and Appendix H run Arditi-style difference-in-means directional ablation as a baseline. It is applied at every layer and position on Qwen3.5-4B, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.7-Flash with thinking enabled. The study reports judge-scored refusal residuals, probe capability passes and MMLU/ARC/IFEval scores against the unedited model. The setting is narrow: fictional adult-content writing refusals, 5-6 fitting probes per model.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors report that directional ablation leaves a small refusal residue on both thinking-disabled models. With thinking enabled it clears all probes, matching L2W at a smaller benchmark cost. They report DA holds baseline benchmark scores in all three configurations. L2W completes removal everywhere but at a substantial benchmark cost on refusal. Their overall conclusion concerns L2W as a general post-editing tool, not the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original difference-in-means direction and projects it out across layers and positions, but replaces the fitting data with the study's refusal probes and matched non-refusal requests. Candidate positions and direction-selection gates are adapted to the study's protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model configuration: directional ablation leaves a held-out refusal residual for both thinking-disabled models but clears the tested probes with GLM thinking enabled. The thinking-enabled direction is selected at the trace-closing token; thinking-disabled directions are selected at the final assistant-template position.

fits_no_version.finding: L2W removes the same adult-content refusal by closing MLP channels, heads or experts. It needs 56-140 components, and benchmark deficits remain (e.g., Qwen IFEval about 23 points below baseline after restoration).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Component-level (non-directional) removal of refusal requires large, capability-entangled cuts, unlike directional ablation.

record.problems: Only three model configurations and small Target-Semantic probe sets (six for Qwen and five for GLM in each configuration) are reported. No uncertainty estimates are given. The study's fitting and selection protocol differs from the original protocol, including its probe sets and suffix-position handling.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper's L2W outcomes are not rows for the directional-ablation claim; direction-selection details are reported as protocol rather than as separately reported outcomes.

untested.parts: Induction by adding the direction is used only as a selection gate on the negative prompts; no induced-refusal rate is reported as an outcome. Refusal of harmful instructions in general is not tested, only refusal of fictional adult-content writing, with 5-6 fitting probes.

Only one reasoning configuration (GLM-4.7-Flash, thinking enabled, trace capped at 2,048 tokens). Whether refusal persists inside the reasoning trace is not judged, since the judge reads the response only. No comparison of direction position beyond the trace-closing token.

record.verdict_notes: The DA results are a baseline in an L2W paper, but they report DA-vs-unedited outcomes, so they bear on V1 and V8. The selection gates (KL ≤0.1 on ablation; adding the direction induces refusal) passed for 5 Qwen and 3 GLM candidates. These are selection values, not outcomes. Probe sets are tiny (5-6 fitting probes, 10 held-out) and no uncertainty is reported, so single residuals may be noise. The original paper's harmful-instruction setting is replaced by adult-content writing refusals.

versions.untested_parts: The reported experiment tests direction removal, not whether adding the direction induces refusal on harmless requests. Its direction fitting and selection use the study's matched prompt sets and adapted suffix-position protocol.
No weight-edit or abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is tested.
The study does not compare an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
Harmfulness judgments and their separation from refusal are not measured.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer of the direction is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is conducted.
The reasoning-enabled test is limited to one model configuration, GLM-4.7-Flash with thinking enabled, and adult-content refusal probes.

relation.reason: DA is the study's baseline, but its own refusal-removal and capability results are reported per model (Table 6, Section 6.5), so they bear on V1 and V8.

tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means recipe with Arditi's gates and selection rule (KL<=0.1, induction gate, least residual refusal), projected out at every layer and position, measured as refusal rate. Only the fitting data and refusal domain differ (Appendix H).

source_check.notes: The refusal here is fictional adult-content writing, not harmful-instruction refusal. The direction is fit on the same 5-6 Psem probes it is scored on, so only Pheld (n=10) is held out; n is tiny and no uncertainty is given. Adding the direction to induce refusal is used only as a selection gate scored from next-token probabilities, with no reported rate, so V1's induction part is untested.

statements.problem: None for this study. Qwen3.5-4B Psem 6/6->1/6 and GLM-4.7-Flash held-out 1/10, thinking disabled, both match Table 6. 'All probes clear' with GLM thinking enabled also matches.

statements.problem: Numbers right. Caveat: the thinking-on/off contrast is a one-probe difference out of 10 and is confounded with direction choice.
